title: Quantum information processing under maximal distance measures
authors: Bartosz Regula, Ludovico Lami, Mario Berta, Marco Tomamichel
abstract: The measures of distance frequently used in quantum information, such as trace distance or fidelity-based purified distance, are the smallest extensions of the corresponding distance measures in classical information theory. However, this way of extending classical distances is not unique, and a whole spectrum of other extensions can be defined. Here we study the question of how quantum information processing tasks are affected by a change of the error metrics to the maximal extensions of the classical distance measures, imposing more demanding error requirements on operational tasks. We find that the performance of some tasks, such as channel coding or quantum resource distillation, is not affected whatsoever by this change. However, for other tasks such as channel simulation and quantum resource dilution, we show that the rates are now given not by functions of the standard (Umegaki) quantum relative entropy, but ones based on the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy. Our results connect the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy with operational tasks and reveal that known reversibility results in quantum information, including the reverse Shannon theorem and the asymptotic reversibility of quantum resource transformations, no longer hold under maximal distance measures.
summary: This work explores the consequences of using 'maximal' error metrics instead of standard ones in quantum information theory. It demonstrates that while some quantum tasks remain robust to this change, others adopt new rate functions based on the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy. Crucially, this shift invalidates several established reversibility theorems in the field.
main_problem: The paper investigates how changing the error metrics used in quantum information processing tasks, from standard minimal extensions to maximal extensions of classical divergences, affects task performance.
main_result: While some tasks (like distillation) are unaffected, others (like channel simulation) are governed by the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy, leading to the breakdown of known reversibility theorems.
method: The authors compare minimal and maximal extensions of classical divergences, utilizing asymptotic i.i.d. limits to calculate task rates and characterizing the variational forms of these maximal divergences.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to general quantum information processing tasks, including channel coding, quantum resource distillation, channel simulation, and quantum resource dilution, using quantum states and quantum channels as the core model.
key_observables: Asymptotic i.i.d. rates for various tasks, the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy, and various maximal divergences ($bT, bP, D_{\max}$).
important_parameters: The choice of error metric (minimal vs. maximal extension) and the specific type of quantum resource transformation being analyzed.
main_assumptions: The maximal extensions are defined by optimizing over all classical distributions and quantum channels; the analysis often requires restricting to Resource-Non-Generating (RNG) operations in resource theories.
figures_summary: Table I compares asymptotic i.i.d. rates for three task types under standard versus maximal distance measures.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the framework by comparing minimal and maximal extensions of divergences. It then analyzes specific tasks (distillation vs. dilution) to show the dependence on the entropy measure. Finally, it extends this to general resource theories and analyzes additivity properties of information measures.
why_interesting: The findings redefine the fundamental quantitative measures of resource costs in quantum information, suggesting that standard theorems relying on simple divergence measures may fail when considering the most general operational constraints.
